anomalies.significance: Info dictionary reveals Chrome browser print-to-PDF; XMP claims MS Word. Document was NOT created by Microsoft Word.
A ModDate that precedes the CreationDate is structurally impossible and is a reliable indicator of manual metadata editing.
Info dict and XMP record different producing software and different modification dates. Both cannot be correct. The Info dict was likely edited manually after creation.
anomalies.iso_reference: ISO 32000-2:2020 §14.3 — both sources should be consistent in a legitimately produced PDF.

exercises.q: What does the Creator field reveal about the true origin of this document?
exercises.a: Creator = Chrome user-agent string. Document was printed to PDF using Google Chrome, not Microsoft Word.

exercises.q: Which metadata source (Info dict or XMP) is more likely to be authentic, and why?
exercises.a: The XMP was injected after initial creation. The Info dict retains the original Chrome/Skia values. Info dict is more likely original; XMP was modified to fabricate a Word origin.

exercises.q: Is the ModDate value valid? What does it indicate?
exercises.a: No. ModDate (Feb 15) precedes CreationDate (Mar 1) — impossible in a normally produced file. Strong indicator of manual hex editing of metadata.

exercises.q: Write the peepdf3 command to display all metadata fields.
exercises.a: peepdf -i lab02_metadata.pdf   then at prompt:   pdf> metadata
